user.title: Add Open Data
user.description: Choose how you want Open Data to find the public data source. Open Data will inspect the source, infer useful fields and data meaning, and create an initial import automatically. You can refine variables, records, timestamp meaning, measurement categories, timezone, and structure later from Configure.

menu_options.local: Find useful data for my area
menu_options.website: Add from a website or dashboard
menu_options.known: Add a known portal, dataset, API, or ID

local.title: Find useful data for my area
local.description: Sources are ranked using your Home Assistant location, formal coverage, practical relevance, and extraction-test history. 'Tested' means the source has actually been exercised by the Open Data extraction corpus; discovered/untested sources may still require new resolver or provider support. Choose a source to let Open Data inspect and import it with inferred defaults; you can adjust the resulting import later from Configure.

website.title: Find the data behind a website
website.description: Paste a public webpage, dashboard, chart, portal, or data page. Open Data will inspect bounded public page evidence for upstream APIs, files, feeds, spreadsheets, and embedded data services without executing arbitrary page JavaScript. If a usable source is found, Open Data will infer an initial import; you can correct variables and categories later from Configure.

resolved_source.title: Choose an upstream data source
resolved_source.description: Open Data found these likely machine-readable sources behind the page. Choose the source that should be inspected next. A resolved source may still require provider/feed support before it can be imported. Successful imports start with inferred settings that remain editable later.

known.title: Add a known data source
known.description: Paste a portal, catalog, dataset page, resource/API URL, or dataset ID. Dataset links import only that dataset; portal roots start bounded catalog discovery. Open Data will infer the initial variables and interpretation automatically, and you can revise them later from Configure.

data.source_location: Portal, dataset, API URL, or ID
data.portal_url: Portal URL for a bare ID (optional)

portal.title: Discover public datasets
portal.description: Enter an institution's public data portal URL. Open Data will prepare and cache the site structure. Large catalogs and file resources can take several minutes; you can leave this screen and return later.

dataset.title: Add a dataset directly
dataset.description: Paste a CKAN or Socrata dataset page, resource/API URL, or dataset ID. A portal URL is required when entering an ID by itself.

data.portal_url: Portal URL for a bare ID (optional)

discover.title: Choose discovered datasets
discover.description: Found {count} ranked datasets on {portal} using {provider}. Select what you want to import. Open Data will infer fields, observation time, freshness, stable records, timestamp semantics, and measurement behavior automatically. The initial choices are not permanent: use Configure afterward to change variables, records, categories, timestamps, timezone, or structure.

prepare.title: Prepare site catalog
prepare.description: Preparing the site catalog in the background. You may close this dialog and return later; no entities or regular downloads begin until you select a dataset.

progress.prepare_catalog: Inspecting the portal, cataloguing datasets, and saving the catalog for later selection

error.cannot_connect: Unable to connect to the supplied source.
error.invalid_reference: The source reference could not be recognized or resolved. Check the URL or provide the portal URL for a bare ID.
error.unsafe_source: The supplied source was blocked by Open Data's network safety checks.
error.invalid_dataset: The portal or selected dataset is invalid.
error.no_datasets: No suitable queryable datasets were discovered on this portal.
error.no_machine_source: No public machine-readable source was found in the bounded page evidence. The page may use an unsupported embed, authenticated API, or JavaScript-only data loading.
error.unknown: Unexpected error. Check the Home Assistant logs.

abort.already_configured: This open data resource is already configured.
abort.no_local_sources: No source profiles in the current audited corpus were relevant to the configured Home Assistant location.

init.title: Adjust inferred fields
init.description: Open Data created the import using automatic inference. Dataset structure: {kind}. The current assignments are preselected below; change only what you want to improve, such as which columns describe location, time, measurements, or context.

structure.title: Adjust units and hierarchy
structure.description: These settings refine an existing import. Define stable units and observations only when automatic structure inference needs correction. Hierarchy sets run from broadest to most specific.

records.title: Adjust imported records and measurements
records.description: These are the current inferred/imported choices. Observation time: {temporal_status} using {timestamp_strategy} ({timestamp_confidence} confidence). Timezone: {timezone} ({timezone_source}). {stale_count} measurements are currently classified stale and are excluded by default unless you select them. Record mode: {record_mode}. This review observed {record_count} records/locations and estimates {entity_estimate} measurement entities from the current bounded selection. If the provider returns the full cardinality cap, Open Data does not show that truncated list as if it were complete.

semantics.title: Adjust what the data means
semantics.description: Open Data inferred these meanings during import. Change them only when the source uses a different meaning. Different clocks and numeric fields can represent observation time, publication time, cumulative totals, interval amounts, event counts, status values, and more. Categories must not overlap.

data.measure_kind_fields__interval_amount: Amounts or volumes for an interval

temporal.title: Adjust timestamp and timezone
temporal.description: Open Data starts with automatic inference. Override it here only if the source's observation time or timezone was misunderstood. A user-selected timestamp field is persisted and reused on every refresh. Enter an IANA timezone such as America/Detroit or Europe/Paris for naive local timestamps.

error.invalid_field_roles: One or more field assignments were invalid. Review the selected fields and try again.
error.invalid_semantics: A timestamp or measurement was assigned to more than one semantic category. Each field can have only one meaning.
error.invalid_timezone: Enter a valid IANA timezone name, for example America/Detroit or Europe/Paris.
error.invalid_timestamp_field: Choose a timestamp field from this dataset.
